about: A Zork-style underground adventure. You wake at the foot of a stair, explore caves, a cliff, a shadow land and a museum, and an old man tests whether you are worthy. A hooded double in the Land of Shadow turns out to be yourself. In the museum, a time machine and a sliding-block puzzle fill out the middle.

done.why: I pushed both ladder blocks in the Royal Puzzle into places I could not move them from, so I could not climb out. Then the world returned a budget-exhausted error.

ending.what: I never reached the old man's stairs. He said I was not yet ready, so I had to gather more first.

moments.note: A hidden watcher at the cliff top chuckles and toys with the rope. It reads as a living presence, and I could not tell what it wanted.
Giving the bread to the sleeping old man opens the secret door.
Going down the stairs turns me back, saying I must gather more elsewhere. The goal is clear but the task is vague.
Fighting the hooded figure and removing its hood shows my own face. The earthquake then opens the museum.
Time machine at 776 strips my inventory and traps me with guards outside. Returning to 948 gives the items back.
The sliding Royal Puzzle let me jam both ladders with no warning or way out. The restart refusal at turn 112 mentioned a rescue that never came.

wished: A way to undo or escape the Royal Puzzle
To explore the other times on the time machine and the Jewel Room
To find out what the Land of Shadow and the lake hide

lines.line: The way down is not yours today. You come back up.
lines.why: It shows the world holds a larger goal, and that I must gather more first.

lines.line: you recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: A strong twist and the best moment of the run.

lines.line: What you have lost stays lost, and what you have done stays done.
lines.why: This is the world's own account of how it works, and it warns that mistakes are permanent.

fun.why: The early exploration, the shadow fight and the time machine were fun. The puzzle trap ended the run badly.

engagement.why: There were many rooms to visit and clear hooks, so I kept going until I was trapped.

difficulty.why: The sliding puzzle is easy to ruin permanently, and nothing warned me.

interestingness.why: Familiar Zork places are mixed with new ideas: the cliff watcher, the lake rule and the self-double.

prose.why: The descriptions are strong. The lake warning and the old man's refusal at the stairs are especially vivid.
